title: No infinite bad tower of full semisimple-kernel quotients
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], with an algebraic closure $\bar k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All group schemes are affine $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroup schemes are closed [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smooth and connected mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Tori and groups of multiplicative type have the meanings of [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type]. For a smooth group $J$, write $\mathfrak j=T_{J/k,e}$ [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space], with bracket induced by commutators [def-wf-lie-algebra]; $\operatorname{Ad}$ is the differential of conjugation. Fix a faithful closed linear representation of $J$ into $\operatorname{GL}_{n,k}$ [def-sc-general-linear-group]. A tangent vector is semisimple if its matrix in this representation is diagonalizable over $\bar k$, and is central if its bracket with every tangent vector is zero. Nilpotent for a group means that it has a finite descending central series of closed normal subgroup schemes with commutators lowering the series. In characteristic $p>0$, $X^{[p]}$ denotes the tangent vector whose left invariant derivation on $k[J]$ is the $p$-fold composite of the derivation of $X$. A restricted Lie subalgebra means a $k$-linear subspace closed under brackets and $X\mapsto X^{[p]}$. A homomorphism is finite faithfully flat when its coordinate algebra is a finite faithfully flat module over the target coordinate algebra; a finite group scheme is infinitesimal if its coordinate algebra is local with nilpotent augmentation ideal. Radicial means universally injective on geometric points. Assume $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$. There is no infinite sequence $(J_i,q_i)_{i\geq0}$ with each $J_i$ smooth, connected and nonnilpotent, every semisimple element of $\operatorname{Lie}((J_i)_{\bar k})$ central, and each $q_i:J_i\to J_{i+1}$ a finite faithfully flat radicial homomorphism whose kernel is central of multiplicative type and has height at most one. Require in addition that $\ker(dq_i)$ is precisely the set of semisimple elements of $\operatorname{Lie}(J_i)$ and that its scalar extension to $\bar k$ is the full semisimple subspace of $\operatorname{Lie}((J_i)_{\bar k})$. Height at most one means that every element of the augmentation ideal of the kernel coordinate algebra has $p$th power zero.

source.place: Proposition 17.80 proof, printed p.378, the sentence beginning "Eventually". This is the termination assertion, separated from construction and torus lifting; Milne refers for its details to Springer 1998, 13.3.5, which is not present locally.

proof.text: Suppose such a tower exists and put $F=\bar k$, $G_i=(J_i)_F$. Connectedness after this extension follows from the identity rational point by [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected], and smoothness from [lem-sfb-scheme-lfp-smooth-flat-base-change]. By [lem-sfb-nilpotence-field-extension], $G_0$ remains nonnilpotent. The coordinate-ring maps after extension are finite (tensor a finite generating set) and faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-base-change]. Kernels are obtained by imposing the same identity-fibre equations after tensoring, so remain central and of multiplicative type. The hypothesis on the geometrically full semisimple kernel says exactly that $d(q_i)_F$ kills every semisimple tangent vector of $G_i$. We henceforth write $q_i$ for these maps over $F$.

source.place: Proposition 17.80, p.378, geometric semisimple-kernel hypothesis; Section 6f and Section 2h for geometric nilpotence.

proof.text: Choose a maximal torus $T_0\subseteq G_0$, allowing $T_0=1$. Here existence requires no conjugacy theorem: take a torus of greatest rank. The ranks are bounded by the dimension $n$ of the given faithful representation: [lem-sfb-split-torus-representation-weight-decomposition] diagonalizes its restriction, and the resulting at most $n$ characters give a closed inclusion into $\mathbf G_m^n$. By [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality], their map $\mathbf Z^n\to X^*(T)$ is surjective, so $\operatorname{rank}T\leq n$. A strict inclusion of split tori increases rank: otherwise its surjective map between free character groups of equal rank is an isomorphism. Now define $T_{i+1}=q_i(T_i)$. By [lem-sfb-quotient-borel-torus-images] these are maximal tori and $f_i=q_i|_{T_i}:T_i\to T_{i+1}$ is faithfully flat.

source.place: Proposition 17.20, pp.357–358; Theorems 12.9, 12.12 and 12.23, pp.233–240; maximal-rank choice is elementary.

proof.text: Every vector in $\operatorname{Lie}(T_i)$ is semisimple in $\operatorname{Lie}(G_i)$: restrict the faithful representation and differentiate its diagonal character blocks, using [lem-sfb-split-torus-representation-weight-decomposition]. Thus $d(q_i)$ kills this tangent space. Choose split coordinates on $T_i$ and $T_{i+1}$. A character pulled back along $f_i$ is a monomial $z_1^{a_1}\cdots z_d^{a_d}$ by [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality]. Differentiating its composite with the faithful diagonal representation of $T_{i+1}$ shows its exponent is divisible by $p$: the weights of that representation generate $X^*(T_{i+1})$ by the closed-inclusion argument of step 2, and each pulled-back weight has differential $(a_1,\ldots,a_d)=0$ in $F^d$. Consequently $f_i^*X^*(T_{i+1})\subseteq pX^*(T_i)$. Composing gives $(f_{r-1}\cdots f_0)^*X^*(T_r)\subseteq p^r X^*(T_0)$. On the subgroup $T_0[p^r]$ defined by $z_j^{p^r}=1$, every such monomial is $1$, so the composite is the identity-valued homomorphism there.

source.place: Theorem 12.12, pp.234–235; character calculation in Theorem 12.9, pp.233–234; Proposition 17.80, p.378.

proof.text: For $r\geq1$ put $Q_r=q_{r-1}\cdots q_0:G_0\to G_r$. Inductively [lem-sfb-multiplicative-isogeny-composition] applies: each $q_i$ is a faithfully flat homomorphism between smooth connected affine groups with finite multiplicative-type kernel, and its conclusion supplies the same hypotheses for the next composition. Thus $\ker Q_r$ is central in $G_0$. Step 3 gives $T_0[p^r]\subseteq\ker Q_r$, hence $T_0[p^r]$ commutes with $G_0$ on every algebra, including nonreduced ones.

source.place: Proposition 18.2 and its proof, p.387, with centrality from Corollary 12.41.

proof.text: The commutator morphism $T_0\times_F G_0\to G_0$ is therefore identity-valued. Indeed, write $T_0=\mathbf G_m^d$, $A=F[G_0]$. For any regular function on the target, the difference of its pullbacks by the commutator and by the constant identity lies in $A[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_d^{\pm1}]$ and restricts to zero modulo $(z_1^{p^r}-1,\ldots,z_d^{p^r}-1)$ for every $r$. Write this finite Laurent sum as $\sum_m a_m z^m$. Choose $p^r$ larger than every absolute nonzero coordinate difference between exponents in its support. Those exponents are distinct in $(\mathbf Z/p^r\mathbf Z)^d$, whose monomials are an $A$-basis of the quotient. All $a_m$ are zero. If $d=0$ the same conclusion is immediate. This proves equality of morphisms, hence centrality on every test algebra, not merely on geometric points. Thus $T_0$ is a central maximal torus. Apply [lem-sfb-central-maximal-torus-nilpotent] to the smooth connected $F$-group $G_0$: it is nilpotent, contradicting step 1.

source.place: Proposition 17.23, p.359; the p-power Laurent-basis density argument is supplied by ND for the termination sentence of Proposition 17.80, p.378.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-ND-f840556de (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, its 5 steps and the new unsplit node lem-sfb-nilpotence-field-extension in full. Milne 17.80 (p.378) only says 'Eventually' and points to Springer 13.3.5, so the delivery supplies its own termination argument, and the argument is sound. Step 1 base-changes to k̄; the cited connectedness, lfp smooth flat base change and faithfully flat base change statements fit their hypotheses. Step 2 bounds torus rank by n using the weight decomposition and antiduality (closed immersion ⇔ surjection on characters), then uses quotient-borel-torus-images to get T_{i+1}=q_i(T_i) maximal with faithfully flat restriction. Step 3: Lie(T_i) is diagonal, hence semisimple and killed by dq_i. Every pulled-back character therefore lies in pX^*, the composite lies in p^r X^*(T_0), and the composite is trivial on T_0[p^r]. Step 4 applies multiplicative-isogeny-composition inductively, which makes ker Q_r central. Step 5: a Laurent-polynomial basis argument over A=F[G_0] shows T_0 is central, and central-maximal-torus-nilpotent then contradicts step 1. The new node is true by Milne 6.38 (pp.133–134) plus the fact that the descending central series commutes with scalar extension (6.19a/§2h). An rg -L search for duplicates found none, and the node is not a clause of the item. Batch 5: the four flagged closures reach generic trf nodes (smooth fibre criterion, exterior-power base change, the scheme-as-algebraic-space definition, the descent-datum definition), all in unit sk-i-curve-zero. None of them is part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality proofs, so I accept them. I accept the two declared tool_uses. No SGA source is cited, and I made no fixes.
